claim: virtual-kubelet imposes no framework-level constraint on what PodIP a provider reports in a virtual pod's PodStatus, or on whether that IP is actually reachable from the cluster network; GetPodStatus returns a plain corev1.PodStatus that the provider constructs however it wants.
stance_target: what pod IP a virtual pod reports and whether it is reachable
quoted_support: GetPodStatus retrieves the status of a pod by name from the provider.

claim: virtual-kubelet's own README states it is explicitly not intended to be an alternative to Kubernetes federation.
stance_target: virtual-kubelet as a multi-cluster federation mechanism
quoted_support: It should be noted that VK is explicitly not intended to be an alternative to Kubernetes federation.

claim: Virtual-kubelet nodes can be incorrectly added to cloud Load Balancer pools by default; the documented workaround requires Kubernetes 1.9+ and enabling the ServiceNodeExclusion feature-gate on the controller-manager to exclude virtual nodes from LB target pools.
scope_conditions: clusters using cloud Load Balancer integration with virtual-kubelet nodes
quoted_support: Kubernetes 1.9 introduces a new flag, ServiceNodeExclusion, for the control plane's Controller Manager. Enabling this flag... allows Kubernetes to exclude Virtual Kubelet nodes from being added to Load Balancer pools.

claim: Among virtual-kubelet providers, Liqo is distinguished by extending real pod-to-pod networking across peered clusters, enabling east-west Service traffic with endpoints reachable on both clusters -- unlike most other providers (e.g. ACI, Fargate) whose virtual pods only proxy execution, not full cluster-network membership.
stance_target: which virtual-kubelet provider architecture actually gives a virtual pod a reachable, cluster-routable IP
quoted_support: The provider combined with the Liqo network fabric extends the cluster networking by enabling Pod-to-Pod traffic and multi-cluster east-west services, supporting endpoints on both clusters.

claim: A virtual-kubelet provider must implement PodLifecycleHandler (CreatePod, UpdatePod, DeletePod, GetPod, GetPodStatus, GetPods) and NodeProvider (Ping, NotifyNodeStatus); the optional PodNotifier interface is recommended for providers running large numbers of pods to avoid virtual-kubelet's default periodic polling of pod status.
stance_target: engineering contract for building a custom virtual-kubelet-backed provider
quoted_support: It is highly recommended to implement PodNotifier, especially if you plan to run a large number of pods.
